facts.value: Applicants are scored on the basis of their best four A-levels, or three A-levels and an AS level in a different subject from the same or preceding year. (note one A-level grade from the previous year may be substituted for an AS grade but will only be scored as an AS).

facts.value: In the case of high demand programmes such as Medicine, a numerus clausus may operate: If there is a significant imbalance in the proportions of eligible applicants for a course between Leaving Certificate and other EU qualifications, places are offered to eligible applicants from each examination system group on the basis of ranking within their group.

source.title: Points to Note:

facts.value: For LM301 Medicine, the requirement is that the score must come from the same sitting in which matriculation is met. For A-level candidates, this means minimum subject entry requirements for the programme must be met in the normal timeframe of GCSE examinations being presented 2 years prior to the A Level results used for scoring.
